subject.title: [Bug]: Feishu streaming card full-content updates cause severe latency regression on long replies

question: Should Feishu keep full-content CardKit updates only and solve latency through coalescing/retry, or add an opt-in append/delta transport mode for deployments that prove CardKit appends correctly?
rationale: Current full-content behavior fixed earlier truncation reports, but fresh live evidence says full-content updates can leave long replies revealing for minutes and the current coalescing PR may not solve that; automation cannot choose the permanent Feishu contract or config surface safely.

options.title: Approve Guarded Append Escape Hatch
options.body: Keep full-content as the default, but allow an explicit Feishu-owned append/delta mode with docs, config/schema tests, and live proof that it improves latency without truncating content in the target tenant.

options.title: Keep Full-Content Only
options.body: Reject append/delta mode and require a full-content repair such as stronger coalescing, body-code retry handling, or final replacement proof before changing defaults.

options.title: Pause Until Better Feishu Proof
options.body: Keep this issue and the linked PR open while collecting gateway logs or production-boundary timing that distinguishes payload-size latency from cadence, rate-limit, and client-rendering issues.

recommendation.title: Approve Guarded Append Escape Hatch
recommendation.body: Keep full-content as the default, but allow an explicit Feishu-owned append/delta mode with docs, config/schema tests, and live proof that it improves latency without truncating content in the target tenant.

likelyOwner.reason: The Feishu plugin metadata names this handle as the community owner, and the decision is specific to Feishu/Lark plugin behavior rather than core runtime architecture.
